record_notes:
Account summary
- PLG-heavy startup (self-serve signup) building an AI coding assistant with a docs/RAG sidecar. Came in through benchmarks content + Github quickstart.
- Using mostly TypeScript/Node. Team is comfortable self-serving but wants fewer “gotchas” during first 15 minutes.
- Evaluation focus: time-to-first-success, streaming UX reliability, and unit cost at moderate concurrency.

What they’re trying to do
- Primary: chat/code-assistant style generation with streaming (interactive UX).
- Secondary: embeddings pipeline for doc-search + lightweight reranking for context selection.
- Wants routing/fallback story later, but first wants one “blessed” default model and a path to upgrade without refactoring.

Requirements (notes from calls)
- Latency: “feels snappy” for IDE plugin; target ~sub-second time-to-first-token when possible; tolerate longer tail for larger prompts.
- Throughput: early stage, but they expect spikes during product launches; wants to understand Dedicated vs Hosted when they hit limits.
- Cost sensitivity: high. They asked for guidance on caching/batching knobs and how to see per-route cost.
- Security: asked for SOC 2 status + audit logs availability. No SSO/SAML requirement yet.
- Data: no regulated data today; still asked how long request metadata is retained and whether they can reduce retention.

Onboarding / activation friction (key insights)
- First 24h: created account + generated API key, but first request failed due to key scope/permissions confusion. They didn’t understand whether the key needed project-level permissions vs org-level.
- Docs mismatch: followed a link that didn’t map cleanly to Console nav; hit a 404 once (they screenshotted it). They later found the correct page.
- Endpoint confusion: they tried completions-style payload against chat endpoint. Their quote: “I just want a copy/paste curl that works; then I’ll read the rest.”
- Streaming: had intermittent disconnect locally; likely proxy-related. They requested explicit troubleshooting steps (timeouts, keep-alive, recommended fetch client settings).
- They liked the idea of a checklist in Console (“API key -> first request -> streaming -> view latency/cost”), especially if it can detect completion and not nag.

Product fit / expansion notes
- If eval passes, likely to ramp usage quickly (PLG motion). They asked about setting budgets/alerts and seeing token spend by route.
- Medium-term: might explore Optimize recommendations and/or Dedicated once they have consistent traffic.

Recent activity timeline
- 2026-01-29: Inbound via self-serve signup; Avery outbound email offering eval guidance + quickstart link.
- 2026-02-06: Technical eval kickoff (Avery + Aparna). Customer shared target UX + current stack (TS/Node). Action items: send “hello inference” snippet + streaming troubleshooting.
- 2026-02-07: Customer reply w/ first-call errors (401/403) + question on key scopes. Aparna sent workaround + asked for screenshots.
- 2026-02-12: Noted a Console navigation/404 issue from email/docs link (flagged as similar to SUP-2841 pattern).
- 2026-02-18: Follow-up call: they got first successful response + tested streaming; asked for cost dashboard pointers and embeddings best-practice.
- 2026-02-21: Customer requested a single-page quickstart that includes: key creation, one curl, one TS snippet, streaming example, and “where to look in Console for latency/cost.”

Aligned next steps (tie-in to lifecycle activation sprint)
- Send activation-focused quickstart variant (copy/paste curl + TS streaming snippet + troubleshooting) and ensure links point to current Console routes.
- Make sure they receive the updated onboarding emails (suppression rules permitting) and monitor whether they complete: api_key_created -> first_request_success -> first_streaming_success -> dashboard_viewed.
- Schedule eval readout end of week: review time-to-first-success, D7 repeat usage, and cost/latency results; decide whether to recommend Hosted API continuation vs start Dedicated sizing conversation.
